6. MENOPAUSE AND MANAGEMENT:

•Average age 50.5years 1 year earlier in smokers
•Perimenopause:

Interval leading to menopause, anovulatory cycle

•Climacteric: period between Reproductive to non-reproductive life.

It includes Menopause.

•POF: < 40years

turner syndrome, Fragile X, Autoimmune Disorders, idiopathic.

1% of women experience POF

•Early menopause < 45 years between age of 40 – 45 yrs.

E and P => FSH Pulsatility

E and P => Menopausal symptoms more in 1st year.

After 1-year estrogen production starts from non-ovarian source leading to reduced symptoms.

Menopause:

When women have no periods for one ear or more between 45 – 55 years.

Diagnosis:

> 45 (No labs) > 40 – 45

Clinical diagnosis based on: > 45yrs

1.Amenorrhea 1 year FSH > 30IU
2.Vasomotor Two levels 4-6
3.symptoms weeks apart.

Clinical Evaluation:

1.Vasomotor Symptoms:
-70% more in 1st year due to pulsatile FSH
2.Urogenital Symptoms:

 

•Genital:
-Itching
-Prolapse
-Dyspareunia 40%
-Atrophy
-Dryness 75%
• Urological 50%
-Nocturia
-Dysuria
-UTI – Recurrent 20%
-Incontinence.
3.Psychological:
-Fatigue
-Depression
-Mood instability
-libido due to Testosterone and atrophy
-Memory loss
-insomnia
4.Osteoporosis:
-More in vertebrae, femur, wrist.
-2% @ 50yrs
-25% @ 80yrs

Diagnosis:

Dexa scan

-T-score comparison with 30yr healthy women
-Z-score among same age group

 

 

T-score

-Normal: -1 to + 1
-Osteopenia: -1 to -2.5
-Osteoporosis: < -2.5

MANAGEMENT OF MENOPAUSE:

→Vasomotor symptoms:

Estrogen replacement therapy ERT

Hormone replacement therapy HRT combined estrogen + progesterone

No uterus

With uterus

1.HRT: offer as 1st line until contraindications
2.SSRI, SNRI, clonidine

Don't offer as 1st line

3.Black cohosh + Isoflavones

No safety data but can improve symptoms.

→Psychological:
1.HRT (consider)
-To improve mood
2.CBT (consider)
-No role of SSRI, SNRI to ease low mood.
→Urogenital atrophy:
1.Vaginal estrogen (offer)

even patients are on HRT to improve local symptoms.

-Consider even if systemic HRT is Contraindicated.
-No relief Dose after advice from expert
-No endometrial thickness monitoring is required with vaginal estrogen.
2.Lubricants:
-For local dryness along with estrogen.
3.If vaginal estrogen and lubricants are not effective/ not tolerated offer vaginal progesterone.
4.If vaginal treatment impractical.

e.g,. disability

Consider ospemifene oral treatment

→Altered Sexual Function:
1.Testosterone.
-consider if HRT alone is not effective.

→Osteoporosis:
1.Prophylaxis
-HRT
-Raloxifene SERM
-Tibolone with GnRH analogue if given for > 6months.
2.Therapeutic
-Bisphosphate + Calcium 1.5g + vitamin D 400 - 600 daily.

1st line: Alendronate if T score is < 2.5.it inhibits osteoporosis

2nd line: Risedronate & Etidronate if T score is - 2.5 - 3 or Alendronate is Contraindications.

3rd line: Strontium Ranelate (2g/day Hs) & Raloxifene if T - score is - 2.5 - 4 or Age > 54.

4th line: teriparatide

 

>40-50% discontinue t/m after 1yr.

>65-75% after 2yrs.

Vaginal Estrogen Deficiency:

-Moisturizer & lubricates - effective in mild-moderate dryness - short term relief of dyspareunia.
-Vaginal E deficiency - short term relief
-HRT
-Laser treatment – can be given to women where estrogen is contraindication.

SERM:

1. Ospemifene

2.Lasofoxifene
-Oral: given where estrogen is contraindicated, licensed for dyspareunia.
3.Tissue selective E complex treatment - oral.
4.Androgens DHEA - oral/vaginal can b given in vulvovaginal atrophy
